title: Trees, Tries, and Ordered Indexes: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Trees, Tries, and Ordered Indexes: Visual Guide

1. Probe Versus Range | THE BRIDGE from hash tables and 'when order matters': toggle point lookup vs range scan over a 1,000,000-key dictionary and drag k, and compare a hash index, an unbalanced BST built from sorted inserts, and a red-black tree; a second toggle explains whichever index you pick | hashing wins the point probe (~1 bucket) and loses the range outright (O(n+k) = 1,000,000+k tests to return 7 matches) while the balanced tree seeks in 20-40 comparisons and follows successors, O(log n + k) - and an unbalanced tree is just the linked list again, height n-1.

2. Fan-Out Beats Depth | drag the internal page size (64 B to 16 KB at 32 bytes per key-pointer entry, so fan-out 2 to 512), switch between 1,000,000 and 1,000,000,000 keys, and toggle 'top 2 levels cached'; the level stack, height, storage reads and comparison count all recompute | height is logarithmic in base fan-out - log256(10^9) = log2(10^9)/log2(256) = 29.9/8 = 3.7, about four page levels versus 30 for a binary tree, and two storage reads once the upper levels are cached; comparisons stay near log2(n) throughout, so the B-tree saves fetches, not comparisons.

3. A Full Leaf Splits | step an insert of key 22 into a full 4-key leaf through all five moves (leaf full, split into two half-full leaves, separator 20 promoted, parent overflows and splits, root split), with a second toggle for classic B-tree vs B+ tree | the unit of rearrangement is a page, not a rotation; a split propagates upward only as far as the overflow reaches, and only a ROOT split changes the height - which is why all leaves stay at the same depth. B+ trees route in the internal pages and link the leaves, turning a range scan into sequential ordered I/O.

4. Walking A Prefix | tap symbols to descend a trie over car, card, care and cat: the current node, whether it is terminal, the live completion set and the highlighted path all update, and three cost bars recompute for the same walk over a 1,000,000-term dictionary | prefix lookup is O(L + k) in the key length and the number of completions - the dictionary size never enters it, so the hash dictionary's 1,000,000-key scan and the sorted array's ~20 boundary comparisons + k are what a trie replaces. Autocomplete for 'car' walks three edges and returns three completions.

5. Merging Equal Tails | switch between a trie and the minimised FST for the keys mop and top, then step the transducer trace symbol by symbol watching the output accumulate | a trie shares prefixes only, so the identical tail 'op' is stored twice (7 nodes, 6 edges); minimisation merges states with identical futures into 4 states and 4 transitions, and an FST hangs outputs (term ID 12 for mop, 37 for top) on the transitions - lookup is still O(L), but the artifact is immutable, built from sorted keys, and updated through overlays and segment merges.
